text.en: It is raining. Afreen and Jyoti watch raindrops slide down the window. Afreen asks, where does all this water come from, and where does it go?

Most of the Earth's surface is covered with water, but most of it is salty. Only a small amount is freshwater.
Imagine all the water on Earth in one glass. The freshwater would be only as much as a teaspoon! The book shows 5 ml of freshwater beside 200 ml of all water.
All living beings, people, animals, birds and plants, depend on freshwater. We need it for drinking, growing crops and our daily activities.
Many plants and animals also live in freshwater. Without water, life would not be possible.
Ocean water is salty, so we cannot drink it. It is useful too. Salt pans of Gujarat dry seawater in flat lands to collect salt; Gujarat is one of the largest salt-producing areas of India.
Freshwater comes from rivers, ponds, lakes and from underground. Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia and helps regulate river flow to prevent floods.
Some animals are made for water. The Fishing Cat of India's wetlands has partly webbed paws and dives for fish.
The Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur is the only floating national park in the world, with floating islands called phumdis and the endangered Sangai deer.

problem.en: Why is only a little of Earth's water useful for drinking?

text.en: Most water is in the oceans.
We cannot drink salty water.
Only a small part is freshwater, so we must save it.

prompt.en: Explain why freshwater is precious although Earth is full of water.

requiredIdeas.en: Only a small amount is freshwater

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all water can be drunk

points.en: Most of Earth's water is salty.
Freshwater is only a small part.
